main_body: Thatched hip roof with a log-plank wall, a framed dark doorway and two round shields below it
top_band: The thatch roof slope runs from about row 7 to row 50 in light ochre (L 124-186). It is laid in horizontal courses with a lighter highlight row at each course edge. Below it the log wall is much darker.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible sloped top surface made of thatch courses, with hipped sides that widen toward the eave. It ends in a lighter, overhanging eave row at about rows 48-54, with a dark shadow under it. Below that is the vertical log wall (rows 55-78) in a much darker tone, well separated from the roof. The doorway is inset with a timber frame, a stone threshold and a dark interior, and a gable cap sits over it. No receding isometric side faces are drawn. This is the same construction as the reference houses.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 lightness steps (L 69, 95, 124, 154, 186) with a highlight row and per-course texture dots. The wall has vertical log grain and the shields have a ring and centre. Outlines are tinted dark brown (only 6% near-neutral dark edge pixels). Flat-fill coverage is 2%, which is low. It carries 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18 for the references, and 38 distinct colours against 66 and 185, so it is somewhat sparser and the thatch courses are repetitive. It still reads as a crafted piece next to the references.
